turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from device physics and training trends

**What works in the training set (top decile, ~19–23%):**
- **Absorbers:** FA-rich mixed halide (FAMAPbBrI, CsFAMAPbBrI, FAMAPbI) — ideal bandgap ~1.55–1.6 eV, good crystallinity, Cs/MA cations suppress δ-phase.
- **n-i-p:** SnO₂ or TiO₂-c/mp ETL + Spiro-MeOTAD (especially with interface passivation layers) + Au. The best row (22.9%) uses the **DM** hole conductor with 2D surface passivation; the 22.0% row uses a passivating interlayer under Spiro.
- **p-i-n:** C60/PCBM + BCP with **PTAA** (Cu or Ag contact) reaches 18–20.3% — a highly selective, low-recombination combination; PEDOT:PSS caps devices ~13–16%.
- Bad news: Sn/Bi/Sb absorbers, wide-gap CsPbBr, carbon electrodes, exotic ETLs → single digits.

**Screening the pool:**

- **c019** — FAMAPbBrI, n-i-p, TiO₂-c/mp, **DM** HTL, Au. DM is the deep-HOMO spiro-analog used in the 22.9% training champion; even without the OAI 2D layer, this stack should be ~20–21%.
- **c079** — FAMAPbBrI, SnO₂-np, **CsPbBr₃-np interlayer | Spiro-MeOTAD**, Au. Interface passivation under Spiro mirrors the 22.0% (CH₃O-PEIA|Spiro) and 19.95% (P3HT with 2D cap) recipes; wide-gap perovskite NPs block electrons and passivate surface traps.
- **c085** — CsFAMAPbBrI, p-i-n, C60|BCP, **PTAA|PFN-Br**, Cu. Direct analog of 20.1% (FTO/C60|BCP/PTAA/Cu) and 18.35/18.15% rows; PFN-Br dipole layer improves wetting and hole extraction.
- **c092** — FAMAPbI, SnO₂-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, MoO₃|Ag, two-step spin. Nearly identical to 19.5% and 19.13% training rows (SnO₂-np/Spiro/Ag or Au); MoO₃ buffer prevents Ag–halide corrosion.
- **c093** — CsFAMAPbBrI, p-i-n, PCBM-60|BCP, PTAA, Ag. Closest analogs at 20.3% (PCBM|C60|BCP/PTAA/Ag) and 20.1%; triple-cation absorber with a highly selective PTAA contact.

Strong runners-up (c008, c034, c038, c047, c062) use similar SnO₂/TiO₂ + Spiro stacks (~17–19% analogs) but lack the extra interface engineering of the picks above.

**Final: c019, c079, c085, c092, c093**
